prompt:
The universe is the integers 1 to 12. The available sets are:
  A = [1, 2, 3, 8]
  B = [1, 4, 6, 9]
  C = [2, 5, 7, 10]
  D = [3, 6, 11]
  E = [4, 5, 12]
  F = [7, 8, 9, 10, 11]
  G = [1, 2, 4, 5, 12]
What is the smallest number of these sets whose union covers the whole universe? Give the final numeric answer. Greedy set cover does not always find the minimum.
checker:
import re
nums = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?\d+\.?\d*', CANDIDATE_OUTPUT)]
# exhaustive over all subsets of the seven sets, smallest covering size
assert any(abs(n - 3.0) < 1e-6 for n in nums), f'3 not found in {nums}'
print('OK')
